order: Add memory files to the Director's authoring exceptions in the guard hook: the project's root memory file and its local sibling, user-level memory under the assistant's config directory (its own memory file plus markdown in memory/memories directories), and any project path matching a new `directorMemoryPatterns` knob in orchestra.json. Memory distills the conversation only the Director holds. Document the exception in the protocol and the README, reusing the plan carve-out's containment discipline: resolved, traversal-checked paths, nothing outside the project or the config directory. Fence it with exactly one rule: simulate each write (Write/Edit/MultiEdit semantics) and deny any result that does not carry the whole managed ORCHESTRA:BEGIN/ORCHESTRA:END block through byte-for-byte — surviving marker lines are not sufficient, the text between them must come through intact too. Keep the denial model-aware and leave every non-memory path blocked as today. Separately add harness versioning: a VERSION file as the single source of truth, stamped by the installer into the protocol header and surfaced by /orchestra-status. Do not change the version format.
claims: The exception covers only the project memory files, config-directory memory, and `directorMemoryPatterns` matches; every other path still falls to default law. The managed block rides through every permitted memory write byte-for-byte — the write is simulated and the result denied unless the block survives unchanged, so markers alone cannot buy an edit through. The denial is model-aware; dormant sessions never see it. Version format unchanged (X.Y.Z), read from the VERSION file only. Verified against the 22-case hook matrix plus an install/re-install/uninstall round-trip.
